item.name: Get the configured default Google project for billing

request.name: Get the configured default Google project for billing

description.content: Get the configured default Google project identifiers that will be used for billing access to requester pays Google buckets. This effectively bills all access to the specified Project and *not* the end-user (may be a different project for different data access methods). If there is no configured default billing project, requests to Data Access Method endpoints will rely on a query parameter `userProject` for the end-user to specify a valid Google project that Fence has the necessary roles in to provide relevant service accounts the necessary access. Please see the README for more details.

response.name: billing projects in response.

Get a list of service accounts for the given Google Cloud Project IDs.
> **NOTE: This will only provide service account information for

will be `0` when the SA isn't currently given access

item.name: Dry run to attempt to update a Google Service Account

request.name: Dry run to attempt to update a Google Service Account

description.content:
Try to update a Google Cloud Project's service account to change access to
controlled data and/or extend access to data WITHOUT actually doing so.
This would extend the service account's access to data if using the non _dry_run
endpoint. It would also modify access if a patch document is provided with new access.

> *NOTE*: If you do not provide a patch document (e.g. no payload),
this will extend access to ALL PREVIOUS DATA. If you want to REMOVE
access, either use the DELETE endpoint or provide a patch document
with an empty list for "project_access". It's important to note that
providing {"project_access": []} is different than not including a
payload at all.

> **WARNING**: Provided patch document will *fully replace* previous data.
It will NOT extend previous data by provided values, it will FULLY
REPLACE the data with what's provided.

query.description: the time (in seconds) during which the Google service account has bucket access. Must be less than the configured maximum (default is 7 days). If it's greater, the configured maximum will be used.

response.name: success, updating service account access is possible
failure, trying to update service account access resulted in errors
unauthorized, can modify provided fields but user does not have permission to update this service account
forbidden, cannot modify the provided fields
